citations.review_text: a joke of a game, launching gives you synchronization errors and then tells me "the product cannot be activated right now" ubisoft is so ass, I should have refunded it when i had the chance to, I'm genuinely baffled at how this company is this bad, no wonder the game was 90% off its because the game doesnt even launch

I bought the game on Steam, launched it, and was immediately told that I needed a Ubisoft account.

Fine. Ubisoft Connect is already one of the worst launchers out there, but whatever. I didn't even have an account before, so I created a brand-new one.

No VPN. No proxy. No network masking. Just a normal internet connection.

The moment I finished creating my account and tried to log in, I was greeted with an "Account Suspended" message. My account had literally just been created. Thinking it was some weird bug, I created another account.

Same result.
 I created a third account. Same result again.

I spent around 20 minutes trying to play a game that I had already PAID for, only to be locked out by Ubisoft's broken account system before I could even reach the main menu.

Requiring a Ubisoft account to play a game I bought on Steam is already annoying enough. But if your account system is so broken that it instantly suspends brand-new accounts for no apparent reason, then maybe it's time to fix your launcher instead of forcing everyone to use it.

I gave up, uninstalled the game, and refunded it.

claims.claim: Players on Nvidia RTX hardware encounter severe graphical issues such as sky and shadow flickering.

citations.review_text: Ok game but there is a bug on RTX 30+ series that causes the shadows to flicker which makes it unplayable for me. It works fine on Steam Deck where I play it the most, but on desktop.. nope.

The game has an graphical issue where the sky begins to flicker which can only be mitigated by using Nvidia Profile Inspector, there's a few tutorials on the Guides tab on the Steam page for more information, if you've been playing Ubisoft games for the PC for a while, this is pretty standard where the port becomes broken overtime with no patches in sight.

Addressing the elephant in the room, the tone has changed drastically from the first game. Characters are a bit lighthearted but the themes of mass surveillance and corporate control hit pretty close to reality. The writing itself is good but the dialogue can feel bad sometimes but it's really subjective on what you can tolerate.

The world of San Francisco feels incredible with more side content, events you can watch and NPCs you can directly interactive with, making the environment feel more alive. The hacking has been improved greatly with more abilities and gadgets that give you an higher advantage in stealth, however once you're detected everyone in the area suddenly knows where you are which is pretty frustrating. 

It's an okay game but I feel like Ubisoft took two steps forward and one back. I can't comment on the multiplayer as I struggled to find a match. The DLCs are okay, mainly customization stuff and a few missions.

Possibly the cringiest dialogue I've ever been unfortunate enough to hear. I'm sure the gameplay is okay at the least, but its impossible to know with the sky strobe lighting you into a seizure, pretty cool that a AAA studio can't make a 10yr old game run on Nvidia.
I love this game but it's nearly unplayable because of the fuⲥⲕing flickering, fix it Ubisoft.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as vibrant and detailed, making exploration of San Francisco enjoyable.

citations.review_text: Watch dogs 1 is a masterpiece. Watch Dogs 2 is a masterpiece covered in gold. This game is amazing, the story is great and the gameplay is so much better, The characters are forgettable besides wrench but the game makes up for that with how alive the open world feels, and how much of an impact you feel like you have on it. I have beat the game and ALL of the DLCs and still keep launching the game up just to play co-op missions with randoms. I wish the randoms would stop leaving the instant I join, but that's not a fault of the game that's a fault of poor sportsmanship in terms of the playerbase. (STOP QUEUEING UP FOR CO-OP MISSIONS IF YOU DON'T ACTUALLY WANNA PLAY CO-OP. YOURE RUINING THE EXPERIENCE OF OTHER PLAYERS YOU A-HOLES)

Watch Dogs 2 is the kind of game that gets better the more you actually play it.
The first thing that stood out to me was the world itself. San Francisco is absolutely gorgeous. The colorful neighbourhoods, beaches, forests, hills, city streets, bridges, suburbs, Silicon Valley areas, and all the little details scattered around the map make the world feel genuinely alive. Even years after its release, I still find myself stopping just to look around or explore places that aren't even part of the main objective.
And visually, the game has aged surprisingly well. The lighting, reflections, weather, sunsets, city atmosphere, and environmental details can make this game look beautiful even today. There are moments where you completely forget that you're playing a game that was released years ago.

The story and characters -

The story is another area where I think Watch Dogs 2 deserves much more appreciation.
It's not trying to be an overly serious, dark revenge story like the first game. Instead, it embraces a much more colorful, youthful, rebellious and playful tone, and I think that's exactly what makes it memorable.
Marcus is a fantastic protagonist, and the DedSec crew gives the game so much personality. Wrench in particular is one of those characters that you will absolutely love. The interactions between the characters, their humour, their personalities, and the way they approach hacking make the story feel like you're actually part of a group rather than simply following a checklist of missions.

The gameplay -

What makes this game so enjoyable is the amount of freedom you're given. You can approach situations in completely different ways.
Hack cameras.
Control security systems.
Manipulate traffic.
Distract enemies.
Use your RC Jumper.
Use the drone.
Create distractions.
Trigger environmental objects.
Stealth your way through an entire area.
Or, if everything goes wrong, just cause absolute chaos.
The hacking isn't just some gimmick attached to the game. It act…

Watch Dogs 2 is a must-buy in my opinion.

It's not GTA, and that's actually one of its strengths. Instead of trying to copy Rockstar's formula, it does its own thing and ends up feeling like a refreshing alternative. The open world is fantastic, with San Francisco being vibrant, detailed, and fun to explore.

The story isn't anything groundbreaking, but it's engaging enough to keep you invested throughout the game. The cast is likable, and the lighter tone works well for the overall experience.

The gameplay is where Watch Dogs 2 really shines. Hacking is far more useful and enjoyable than it was in the first game, giving you plenty of creative ways to approach missions. Whether you prefer stealth, using gadgets, or causing chaos from a distance, the game offers a lot of freedom.

Most importantly, it's a major improvement over the original Watch Dogs in almost every way. Better gameplay, a more enjoyable world, and a more entertaining overall experience.

If you're looking for a fun open-world game with unique mechanics, Watch Dogs 2 is absolutely worth picking up.

claims.claim: Reviewers report unexpected application crashes during gameplay.

citations.review_text:
It's a good game, however, there are some things that can just really annoy you. Can't jump, only parkour when it decides you can and its very very hit or miss, like I can vault something but I'm smashing space and its not doing anything. The animations for this also REALLY slow down gameplay and can get you in trouble if you're trying to move quickly. I don't need a fancy backflip when I'm running from 2 different gangs at the same time. Using cover is cool, until it doesn't release like its supposed to by moving. Just make a button to leave cover. The entering hacker space animations, method of sleeping to save, etc. all take a ridiculous amount of time for something that should take 2 seconds. Key response, especially during gun fights can get you killed because it just decides not to register sometimes, especially if you need to be doing multiple things at once, you just end up standing there like an idiot getting shot. Lastly, for whatever reason, my game recently started crashing, like a lot, and it seems to be if the Nvidia control panel is active in taskbar. I exit it 3-4 times before it finally stays closed and then my game seems to stop crashing. Not sure what that's about. 

Now, with all that said, I'm still saying id recommend this game. It's got a pretty good story, lots of missions, side missions, and even DLC missions you can do and they're for the most part, very enjoyable, and at times challenging. There's also a lot of things you can collect around the city which adds little challenges as you're driving around. Driving is mid but they at least made it so it feels like it was designed for keyboard players which is nice, however some cars are just not that great to drive, and most are the faster cars in the game.
